problem: Existing audio-visual navigation (AVN) agents generalize poorly to unheard sound categories and unseen scenes: audio encoders entangle semantics with spatial cues, and RL policies overfit to training-environment dynamics and layouts, causing oscillation and backtracking.
motivation: Sound semantics are unreliable under category shift and obscure universal localization cues. Interaural differences are category-agnostic, and action-transition regularities are shared across environments. Exploiting both should improve zero-shot generalization in a plug-and-play way.
key_idea: Add a Binaural Difference Attention module that weights left/right audio features by their interaural difference, plus an auxiliary next-action prediction loss (ATP) as a policy regularizer, to existing AVN backbones.
insight: Both parts contribute on AV-NaV/Replica (Table ablation). Unheard SR is 47.3 with neither, 66.2 without ATP, 63.4 without BDA, and 68.6 with both. The lambda sweep (ATP only) shows Unheard SR rising from 47.3 (λ=0) to 63.4 (λ=0.1), so the auxiliary action-transition task alone provides large regularization gains. Gains are largest on unheard sounds, which supports the claim that difference-based spatial cues and transition regularization reduce reliance on semantics and environment-specific overfitting.
method: Encoders: two independent CNN encoders (8x8, 4x4, 3x3 convs + linear) on the depth image and binaural spectrogram give 512-d visual and audio features, as in AV-NaV.
BDA input split: the binaural spectrogram is split into left/right channels and encoded by a weight-shared CNN into feature maps f_al and f_ar, inside the audio encoder before the linear layer.
BDA fusion: diff=|f_ar−f_al|; concat(f_al,f_ar) goes through a 1x1 conv and sigmoid to give w; f_a = f_al⊙(1−w)⊙diff + f_ar⊙w⊙diff, so the difference modulates the channel weights.

ATP auxiliary task: a two-layer FC AuxNet takes [s_t; onehot(a_t)] and predicts the next action a_{t+1}, trained with cross-entropy over rollouts (N=4 for AV-NaV, N=81 for the AV-WaN 9x9 waypoint map).
Joint objective: L_total = L_PPO + λ L_aux with λ=0.1, applied plug-and-play on AV-NaV and AV-WaN.

setting.backbone: AV-NaV and AV-WaN style CNN encoders + recurrent PPO policy, with BDA and ATP added (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: SoundSpaces audio-visual navigation training scenes on Replica and Matterport3D with heard sound categories; no extra data
setting.action_space: AV-NaV: discrete Forward/Left/Right/Stop; AV-WaN: waypoints on a 9x9 action map

numbers_note: The paper does not name the official split; 'test' is assumed for the unseen-scene evaluation. SoundSpaces AVN has no canonical benchmark name in the list, so 'other:' names are used.
results: BDATP consistently improves AV-NaV and AV-WaN on Replica and Matterport3D. On Replica, AV-WaN+BDATP reaches 96.5 SR Heard and 70.7 SR Unheard, beating SA2GVAN (62.8 Unheard). AV-NaV Unheard SR rises by 21.3 points on Replica (47.3→68.6) and by 21.6 on Matterport3D (33.5→55.1). ORAN still leads on some SPL/SNA entries.
limitations: Only two baselines (AV-NaV and AV-WaN) are augmented; ablations are only on AV-NaV/Replica, and evaluation is simulation only.
No full ablation on Matterport3D or on AV-WaN; the λ ablation is run without BDA, and the ATP rationale is heuristic.
SNA/SPL do not always beat ORAN; no real-robot or dynamic-sound evaluation.
